And they were seeking to lay hold on him, and they feared the multitude, for they knew that against them he spake the simile, and having left him, they went away;
and they send unto him certain of the Pharisees and of the Herodians, that they may ensnare him in discourse,

and they having come, say to him, 'Teacher, we have known that you are true, and you are not caring for any one, for you do not look to the face of men, but in truth the way of God do teach; is it lawful to give tribute to Caesar or not? may we give, or may we not give?'
And he, knowing their hypocrisy, said to them,
and they brought, and he said to them, this image, and the inscription?' and they said to him, 'Caesar's;'
and Jesus answering said to them, and they did wonder at him.
And the Sadducees come unto him, who say there is not a rising again, and they questioned him, saying,
'Teacher, Moses wrote to us, that if any one's brother may die, and may leave a wife, and may leave no children, that his brother may take his wife, and raise up seed to his brother.
'There were then seven brothers, and the first took a wife, and dying, he left no seed;
and the second took her, and died, neither left he seed, and the third in like manner,
and the seven took her, and left no seed, last of all died also the woman;
in the rising again, then, whenever they may rise, of which of them shall she be wife -- for the seven had her as wife?'
And Jesus answering said to them,
the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob;
And one of the scribes having come near, having heard them disputing, knowing that he answered them well, questioned him, 'Which is the first command of all?'
and Jesus answered him -- , Hear, O Israel, the Lord is our God, the Lord is one;
the first command;
like , this, You shall love your neighbor as yourself; -- greater than these there is no other command.'
And the scribe said to him, 'Well, Teacher, in truth you have spoken that there is one God, and there is none other but He;

and to love Him out of all the heart, and out of all the understanding, and out of all the soul, and out of all the strength, and to love one's neighbor as one's self, is more than all the whole burnt-offerings and the sacrifices.'
And Jesus, having seen him that he answered with understanding, said to him, and no one any more did question him.
And Jesus answering said, teaching in the temple,
and he was saying to them in his teaching,
And Jesus having sat down across from the treasury, was beholding how the multitude did put brass into the treasury, and many rich were putting in much,
and having come, a poor widow did put in two mites, which are a farthing.
